title: The work list
dek: What is being done here, as opposed to what is known.
lead: Every other register on this site answers what this archive knows. /searched/ holds every query ever run, /open-questions/ holds what is not known, /errands/ holds what can only be got through a door, and /corrections/ holds what was got wrong. None of them answers what is being DONE — and so for weeks that lived in a chat window, which is the one place that does not survive the session. This page is that list. It is deliberately not a list of findings. It is who is doing what, who is waiting on whom, and what was decided against and why.
close: An item here with no owner would be wallpaper, so the build refuses one. An item that has been open for six weeks is marked as such rather than left to look like something raised this morning.

rows.what: Sweep the Transvaal education series (TAB, source OD) for every surname and farm this archive holds
rows.note: One accidental query — **BOOYZEN AND MARICO** — returned a farm school at Kwaggafontein with a JGL Booyzen on eight of its forty-eight files, and a second school on this family's own farm at Vaalbank. Neither was looked for. The series has never been searched for **BARRY**, **MOUNTJOY**, **DASCHNER** or **KOLBE**, nor for Brakfontein, Koedoesfontein, Driefontein, Zwartruggens or Goedehoop. [What was found](/documents/#kwaggafontein-school) **15 September, paused:** NAAIRS answers «the connection to the Search Manager Server is inactive». Not a negative about anything — an outage.

rows.what: Finish reading the two school files — 28 of 72 Kwaggafontein documents, 30 of 54 at Vaalbank
rows.note: The unread half of Vaalbank is where the **Ds. Booysen** question lives: whether that abbreviation is a pair of initials, David Schalk, or the Dutch for a minister. The index will not settle it; the file might. **Parked by the same outage.**

rows.what: Sweep the eGGSA newspaper transcriptions for the four surnames that have never been put through them
rows.note: **KOLBE** was swept properly for the first time today: 43 hits, read one at a time, and it produced Francis McCabe, the location of the farm, a son of the twelve, and the Settler's mission school. **BOOYZEN, BARRY, MOUNTJOY and DASCHNER have never had the same treatment.** The search endpoint is now scriptable, so this is an hour's work rather than a day's. [Today's run](/documents/#mccabe-1872) **Done, 15 September.** Daschner returns nothing in the whole collection; Booyzen five and Booijsen one, almost all of it other families; and MOUNTJOY gave the thing this archive did not expect — a man who lodged in James Mountjoy's house in January 1822 and recorded that he was **discharged from the 21st Light Dragoons**. [What it broke](/documents/#mountjoy-dragoons)

rows.what: Find Francis McCabe's own estate at the Free State depot
rows.note: He was **Landdrost of Bloemfontein** and died on 23 February 1872 leaving «a widow, four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children». Those step-children are the Commandant's twelve. His file would name them — reaching the same list from the opposite side to VAB MHG M777, which is not readable online. **Parked by the same outage.**

rows.what: Bring /open-questions/ up to date — §0 is a day behind and the letters section is three days behind
rows.note: §0 still ends «the next step is the Graaff-Reinet baptism register for 21 September 1788». It does not know that the 1981 revision was confirmed this morning, that no Gerhardus Lodewicus married a Magdalena de Beer, or that the disputed name sits nine lines lower on the same sheet as a son. The page also still calls NAAIRS «the single most important unopened door», which stopped being true three weeks ago. [Question 0, as it now stands](/documents/#question-zero) **Done, 15 September.** §0 now carries the 1981 confirmation, van Zyl's failed marriage search, the son on line 12 and the closed FamilySearch route. §12 is rewritten around the Light Dragoons and moved from Blocking to High. The letters section says Pretoria answered.

rows.what: Read the rest of de Villiers's volumes 2 and 3 for the surnames not yet looked up
rows.note: Volume 2 gave Anna Maria van der Merwe her baptism and six siblings; volume 3 gave Adriana Christina Viljoen her parents and made her David Schalk's first cousin. Not yet looked up: the van der Merwe siblings' own descendants, the de Beer entry, the five **Dormehl** mentions, the Oliviers, and the six **Slier** entries in volume 3 which may be Anna Catharina Slier. [What volumes 2 and 3 gave](/documents/#kaapsche-2-3) **Done, 15 September.** The six Slier entries turned out to be a whole family: **Willem Slier of Hamburg** and **Anna Catharina Fortman**, married 1780, and their daughter baptised 14 October 1787. Two pages on, the Pietersens — which showed this archive had been running a husband and his son under one name. Dormehl is in volume 2 and is ninety years too early to connect. [What it gave](/documents/#slier-pietersen)

rows.what: Engage the private researcher at Pretoria, or decline — six bound estate files, fees not yet known
rows.note: The National Archives answered that **all six MHG files are bound** and cannot be scanned and emailed, and put a private researcher who specialises in estate files on copy. She was written to today and asked what she charges, how, and whether the work is worth doing at all, with an offer to start with one file. **This is money, so it is David's to decide and not this archive's.** If she charges per page, MHG 3734/46 is the one to buy first: Catherine Mary Sophia Daschner's notice should name the parents this archive still cannot prove. [The files](/errands/)

rows.what: Sign in to FamilySearch
rows.note: Four pieces of work are parked behind one sign-in. The **Burgersdorp baptism register sweep is stopped at image 604 of 818**; the whole-film nameless sweep has not begun; three Kolbe children and Angeline of Wakkerstroom are unfollowed; and the phthisis reading on Henry James Booyzen's death record is unchecked. Nothing else on this list is waiting on so little.

rows.what: Send the Pietermaritzburg letter, or telephone first — the email address is in doubt
rows.note: Six Natal estate files, drafted and deliberately unsent. The National Archives' own record gives **pmbarchives@dact.kzntl.gov.za** on an entry last touched in 2015, and kzntl.gov.za is a retired domain; other listings give **pmbarchives@kzndac.gov.za**. The postal address and the telephone, 033 342 4712, agree across every source. This archive has already posted one enquiry into a mailbox it could not confirm and will not do it twice.

rows.what: MOOC 8/18.11 entire — the 1781 inventory that names eleven enslaved people
rows.note: **The heaviest thing on this list.** The index line names Silvia, Lena, Sara, Janna, Dorinda, Fortuijn, Meij and Februarij van de Caab, Dijk and Farla van Madagascar, and Achilles van Mallabaar, in the estate of Gerrit Booijsen at Drakenstein. TANAP transcribed these inventories in full and **its database no longer resolves**, with the Internet Archive down as well, so there is no screen route left at all. What is wanted is the document: every name and valuation, and the heirs — because if the heirs include a Jan, this archive's direct line runs through it. [What the index line says](/documents/#mooc8-inventories)

rows.what: Two letters to the Western Cape Archives, sent and unanswered
rows.note: The Mountjoy wills and the Colonial Office memorial went on 9 September; the Lerena death notice on the same evening. Six days, no reply. Not yet chased, because a reading room that has had one working week is not late.

rows.what: Decide whether a gendatabase.com subscription is worth buying
rows.note: The boundary is now known exactly. **Free**: names, surname, date of birth, baptism date. **Paid**: baptism place, source, image, entry number, father, mother, parents. The free layer gives dates and the paid layer gives parentage — and this archive has most of its dates and is starved of parents. One specific question would be settled by one record: whether the Johanna Catharina Mountjoy born 28 January 1860 was baptised in the Barkly East district, which would make her the woman who died at Indwe in 1911. [What it gave for nothing](/documents/#gendatabase-two)

rows.what: One address at the SANDF Documentation Centre bounced and has not been replaced
rows.note: The enquiry about UDF service and pension records went to two addresses. **sandfdoc@mweb.co.za returned 550 relay access denied**; archive@dod.mil.za did not bounce and has not answered. Half-delivered is recorded as half-delivered rather than as sent.

rows.what: The letters are tracked in three places and no single one shows what is outstanding
rows.note: Outgoing correspondence is split between prose on [/open-questions/](/open-questions/), entries in the research log, and files in the requests folder. Six enquiries are live right now, and reconstructing that took a search of an inbox rather than a look at this site. **This list is the first half of the fix**; the letters themselves still need one register. **Done, 15 September:** [/letters/](/letters/), eight enquiries with what came back, linked from the menu.

rows.what: Find the 21 September 1788 baptism through the FamilySearch Dutch Reformed collection
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake about the collection and kept here rather than deleted.** The plan was to locate the register holding Petrus Jacobus Booijsen's baptism and read it, which would name his father in a contemporary hand and end the oldest question on this site. The Baptism Finder was asked which registers exist for Paarl (Drakenstein), Graaff-Reinet and Stellenbosch: 54, 48 and 55 — and **sorted earliest first, the first row in every town is 1843**. It is the post-1842 church archive series and it does not reach the eighteenth century at all. The question is unchanged and the route never existed. It is a Cape Town errand now. [Why the route closed](/documents/#gendatabase-two)

rows.what: Read the seven Marico war-compensation files at a screen
rows.note: **Two days were spent treating these as a lead that could be worked online.** All seven detail records were finally pulled today and every one reads, in full, «CLAIMS FOR COMPENSATION BURGHERS. MARICO. XX BOOYZEN.» No remarks, no farm, no forename, no amount. **The index line is the whole record** and no screen anywhere will improve it. Struck as a screen task and moved to [/errands/](/errands/), which is where a thing belongs when the only remaining step is a door.

rows.what: Chase the London tailor into a directory through Google Books
rows.note: Whether John Godloff Kolbe of the 1844 obituary was at **Brunswick Square** or at **34 Conduit Street** is still open. The books API returns HTTP 429 with a daily quota of zero for anonymous callers, so that route is shut and a different one is needed — archive.org full text, HathiTrust, or londonancestor.com. One thing did come out of it and is not being claimed: a list of 234 London master tailors who met over the Combination Act on 22 December 1799 includes «KOLBE, JOHN, 18, BROAD-STREET, SOHO». Right trade, right city, right age, and Soho was the German quarter — but a John Kolbe in London is not yet this John Kolbe. **15 September, the other routes tried and closed.** HathiTrust is behind Cloudflare bot protection and **this archive will not go around that**. archive.org holds no London trade directory earlier than 1920. The 1810s-to-1840s directories are on the paid genealogy services and at the Guildhall Library and London Metropolitan Archives, and nowhere free. **Now genuinely a door question, and the door is in London** — which is where WO 97 is too, so the two travel together.

rows.what: Tell the estate that the FamilySearch Dutch Reformed baptism films begin in 1843
rows.note: **This belongs to every archive here, not to this one.** Any archive working Cape Dutch Reformed registers through FamilySearch has the same ceiling and may, like this one, be reading its silence as absence rather than as the edge of a filming project. It explains retrospectively why weeks of work on this family produced nothing older than the 1840s. The originals exist; they are at Cape Town.

rows.what: Offer the estate two search techniques worked out here
rows.note: Both are general and neither is written down anywhere shared. **NAAIRS** can be driven end to end from a page — the rotating token, the database selector, the POST that must carry its AND operators explicitly, and the detail endpoint — which turns a frameset nobody can script into a few seconds per query. And the **eGGSA newspaper index** is an Elasticsearch behind a widget: its query shape takes a fragment count, so one request returns every mention in every transcript rather than the one the widget draws.

rows.what: The archive-kit pin was four commits behind and this page is why we noticed
rows.note: This archive was pinned to **b16bea79** and the work list component, its checker and the estate roll-up were added after it. Diffed before bumping — seven files, 658 insertions, nothing removed and nothing this build depends on touched — then moved to **60aad580**. Recorded because an archive silently behind on the shared kit is the same failure this page exists to prevent, one layer down.

rows.what: Reply to Pieter van Zyl and Riël Smit on WikiTree — they answered the oldest question on this site and have not been told what it produced
rows.note: Riël Smit confirmed from the **1981 edition this archive does not own** that Petrus Jacobus is still placed under Jan, and Pieter van Zyl searched for a marriage between a Gerhardus Lodewicus and a Magdalena de Beer, found none, and remembered from the notice itself that a **child** of Petrus Jacobus carried the name — which turned out to be nine lines lower on the same sheet. **Two people did unpaid work for this archive today and neither has been thanked or shown the result.** The reply is this archive's to draft and David's to post; posting is public writing under his name, not something this archive does for him. [What they settled](/documents/#question-zero) **Drafted 15 September** and sitting in the requests folder, unposted. It reports what their answers produced, says plainly what this archive has *not* done — the chart still shows Gerthardus Lodewikus at the top — and asks them the one question left: whether the pre-1843 Drakenstein doopregisters have been transcribed or filmed anywhere this archive has not thought of. It also gives something back, since both of them work these families.

rows.what: A build check that every event on the atlas carries a citation
rows.note: The Marico entry carried «1898 — JGL Booyzen of Kwaggafontein, in the field-cornet's papers» for weeks. The papers were the education department's, and the line survived because **nothing on the site pointed at it** — no page cited it, so no page could contradict it. An event nobody can check is an event nobody can correct. The other registers here are already gated: the kit check, the living-person rule, and now the work list. **The atlas is the one register with no gate**, and it is the one that was wrong. [The correction](/corrections/) **Done, 15 September.** `tools/checkatlas.py`, in build.sh after links.py. It refuses a build where a place pinned approximate carries no «why», and warns where a place with events is discussed nowhere on the site. **First run: eighteen failures**, every one a farm pinned near its district with nothing saying so. All eighteen now state what the pin rests on and several say outright that it is weak.

rows.what: File today's leads into /open-questions/ and /errands/ so they stop living on this page and in a chat window
rows.note: This list is for what is being **done** and it is already carrying things that are really research leads — which is how it would turn into a second, worse copy of the registers it sits beside. Nine of them came out of today and have no home yet: the Volksraad of May 1867; the twelve remaining Booijsen inventories at MOOC8; the eight Kolbe sons through the National Archives Discovery catalogue and the German Savoy RG4 registers; the Kolbe-Booysen household at Port Elizabeth; «little Jannie» of 1884, whom two papers give two fathers; **Jephts of Leeuwberg**, the man of colour the 1869 court named with property of his own; and the Settler's Bushman mission school at Koolskop. **Each belongs in a register that already exists.** Moving them is the work; keeping them here is the drift. **Done, 15 September, and here is where each went.** §15 of [open questions](/open-questions/) is new and holds **the Commandant's twelve children**, with John Kolbe junior as the one document has reached and the thirty-one tree names explicitly refused. [Errands](/errands/) gains the **Volksraad minutes for May 1867** and **Francis McCabe's own estate** under the Free State depot, and the **twelve remaining Booijsen inventories** under Cape Town. **Kew is a new depot** on the same page. The Kolbe-Booysen household, «little Jannie» of 1884 and Jephts of Leeuwberg are written up in the documents and carried in [what has been read](/searched/), which is the register for a lead nobody is working yet.
